verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The Lean reaches '→ +∞' by a different route and at a different point, and never states the asymptotic identity. (i) Component: the paper diverges in the angular component U_θ at the off-axis point λ⁻¹√ν x_τ; the Lean divergence is of the full norm ‖U(t,x)‖ and is produced at the spatial origin x = 0, where the constructed field is axial — coreVelocity (t,0) = ((1-t)^{-A} j) • coordinateVector 2, the third (axial) basis vector, and MixedAxisPreservation.final_speedUnbounded (line 527) likewise routes through NaturalCore.speedUnbounded_of_axis_tendsto at x = 0. (ii) Form: the Lean conclusion is the quantified unboundedness SpeedUnboundedAtOne, not an asymptotic equality; no expansion τ^{-A}(e_0 + O(τ^{2h})) for the periodic field appears — the error term O(τ^{2h}) has no counterpart here, and the Lean axis law (1-t)^{-A}·j is an exact equality with no correction. (iii) Amplitude: the factor λ√ν is not displayed; it appears as two separate norm-scaling steps, ×√ν in rescale_speed_unbounded and ×l = λ in velocity_speed_unbounded, each of which only has to beat an arbitrary threshold M. What the paper uses this display for later ('contradicts the boundedness of the smooth v on a compact neighborhood of (0,1)') is exactly SpeedUnboundedAtOne, which the Lean does supply for the periodized field, so the surrounding corollary is still proved.
